name: rename-wide
prompt: Rename the function textutil.Plural (internal/textutil) to PluralSuffix, everywhere it is used. Behaviour must not change.
check: go vet ./... && ! grep -rn --include=*.go --exclude-dir=testdata 'textutil\.Plural(' . && grep -q 'func PluralSuffix' internal/textutil/*.go && go test ./internal/textutil/ ./internal/edits/...

name: add-parameter
prompt: edit.Unified (internal/edit/diff.go) always shows 3 lines of context. Give it an int parameter for the number of context lines, use it instead of the 3, and pass 3 at every call so behaviour does not change.
check: go vet ./... && grep -Eq 'func Unified\([^)]*int\)' internal/edit/diff.go && ! grep -q 'group(ops, 3)' internal/edit/diff.go && go test ./internal/edit/ ./internal/workspace/

name: extract-function
prompt: In internal/refactor/refactor.go, Run builds the refusal message for a step that broke the build in two ways, depending on whether the step is an Edit. Extract the code that builds that message into a function named rollbackReason. Behaviour must not change.
check: go vet ./... && grep -q 'func rollbackReason' internal/refactor/refactor.go && go test ./internal/refactor/...

name: small-edit
prompt: In internal/locate/locate.go, change the refusal "file is required" to "file is required: a path relative to the module root".
check: go vet ./... && grep -q 'file is required: a path relative to the module root' internal/locate/locate.go && go test ./internal/locate/

name: rename-field
prompt: Rename the Summary field of refactor.Plan (internal/refactor/refactor.go) to Headline, everywhere it is used. Other things named Summary, such as the Summary field of refactor.Result, keep their names. Behaviour must not change.
check: go vet ./... && grep -Eq '^\s+Headline\s+string' internal/refactor/refactor.go && grep -Eq '^\s+Summary\s+string\s+.json:"summary' internal/refactor/refactor.go && go test ./internal/refactor/... ./internal/mcpserver/ ./internal/eval/

name: add-parameter-nested
prompt: Add a parameter suffix string to textutil.Plural (internal/textutil), after n, and return it instead of the hard-coded "s". Pass "s" at every call so behaviour does not change.
check: go vet ./... && grep -Eq 'func Plural\(n int, [A-Za-z]+ string\) string' internal/textutil/textutil.go && ! grep -q 'return "s"' internal/textutil/textutil.go && go test ./internal/textutil/ ./internal/edits/... ./internal/refactorings/changesig/ ./internal/refactorings/extractfunc/

name: move-to-package
prompt: Move the helper function limit from internal/refactor/refactor.go into package textutil (internal/textutil) as the exported function Limit, and update its callers. Behaviour must not change.
check: go vet ./... && grep -q '^func Limit' internal/textutil/*.go && ! grep -q '^func limit' internal/refactor/refactor.go && go test ./internal/refactor/... ./internal/textutil/

name: story-option
prompt: Refusals from refactor.Run (internal/refactor/refactor.go) list at most 10 type errors. Add a field MaxErrors int to refactor.Options so a caller can choose that limit, with 0 meaning the current 10, and use it in every place the 10 is used now. Callers that do not set it must behave as before.
check: go vet ./... && grep -Eq '^\s+MaxErrors\s+int' internal/refactor/refactor.go && ! grep -q 'limit(errs, 10)' internal/refactor/refactor.go && go test ./internal/refactor/... ./internal/mcpserver/

name: multi-plural
prompt: Three changes to textutil.Plural (internal/textutil): rename it to PluralSuffix everywhere; give it a parameter suffix string after n, returned instead of the hard-coded "s", with "s" passed at every call; and move it into a new file internal/textutil/plural.go. Behaviour must not change.
check: go vet ./... && grep -Eq '^func PluralSuffix\(n int, [A-Za-z]+ string\) string' internal/textutil/plural.go && ! grep -q 'return "s"' internal/textutil/plural.go && ! grep -q '^func Plural' internal/textutil/textutil.go && ! grep -rn --include=*.go --exclude-dir=testdata 'textutil\.Plural(' . && go test ./internal/textutil/ ./internal/edits/... ./internal/refactorings/changesig/

name: multi-move-rename
prompt: Two changes: move the helper function limit from internal/refactor/refactor.go into package textutil (internal/textutil) as the exported function Limit, updating its callers; and rename the function refactor.Refusef to Refuse everywhere it is used. Behaviour must not change.
check: go vet ./... && grep -q '^func Limit' internal/textutil/*.go && ! grep -q '^func limit' internal/refactor/refactor.go && grep -q '^func Refuse(' internal/refactor/refactor.go && ! grep -rn --include=*.go --exclude-dir=testdata 'Refusef(' . && go test ./internal/refactor/... ./internal/locate/ ./internal/textutil/

name: multi-fields
prompt: In internal/refactor/refactor.go: rename the Notes field of refactor.Plan to Caveats everywhere it is used (the Notes field of refactor.Result keeps its name), and add a field Warnings []string to refactor.Result just after its Notes field, with the tag `json:"warnings,omitempty"`.
check: go vet ./... && grep -Eq '^\s+Caveats\s+\[\]string' internal/refactor/refactor.go && grep -Eq '^\s+Notes\s+\[\]string\s+.json:"notes' internal/refactor/refactor.go && grep -Eq '^\s+Warnings\s+\[\]string\s+.json:"warnings,omitempty"' internal/refactor/refactor.go && go test ./internal/refactor/... ./internal/mcpserver/

name: feat-symbol-addressing
prompt: The refactoring tools that target a declaration (rename, add_parameter, remove_parameter, move_parameter, move_declaration, function_to_method, method_to_function, remove_dead_code, merge_duplicate_function, extract_struct, add_field) identify it by file, line and name. Let them also accept file and name without line: name is then a package-level symbol of file's package, declared in any of its files: a function, type, variable or constant ("Name"), or a method or struct field ("Type.Method", "Type.Field"). They all find their target through locate.Ident (internal/locate), so it is enough that locate.Ident, given an IdentQuery whose Line and Column are both 0, resolves Name that way; a Name that is no such symbol must give a *refactor.Refusal. Addressing by line must keep working, and the tools' input schemas should no longer require line.

name: feat-case-clause
prompt: replace_statements (internal/edits/replacestmts) cannot replace the whole body of a case clause: given the lines of every statement after a `case x:` line, it refuses, saying the selection cuts the clause. Selecting all of a case clause's body statements, without its `case x:` line, should be allowed and replace just the body. Selecting the `case x:` line itself is still not allowed.

name: feat-no-echo
prompt: When create_file or add_declaration (MCP tools served by internal/mcpserver) apply, their result is a diff that repeats, line by line, the code the model just sent, which costs the model tokens to read again. Change those two tools' results so that code the model supplied is not repeated: say instead how many lines were added and which lines they are now (for example "lines 1-6"). Lines the tool adds itself, such as an import it added, must still be shown. Other tools' results do not change.

name: feat-compact-diffs
prompt: The MCP server's refactoring and edit results (internal/mcpserver) show a unified diff with three lines of context around each change. The context costs the model tokens and it rarely needs it. Make the MCP server's results show only the changed lines, with hunk headers that still say where they are. The refactor command-line tool (cmd/refactor) should keep showing three lines of context.

name: design-duplication
prompt: The exports in package export (CSV, JSON and Markdown) leave out pending orders. They must also leave out cancelled orders, and list the orders by customer name, then by ID, instead of by ID alone.

name: design-tangled
prompt: Add a customer kind "partner" (Order.CustomerKind == "partner") to pricing.Total: partners pay wholesale's unit price (20% off) but get none of the quantity discounts, and they pay tax as retail customers do (20%, or 18% when the subtotal is over 100000 cents). Other customers' prices do not change.

name: design-currency
prompt: The exports in package export write amounts as dollars and cents. Make them use the shop's currency: add a type export.Currency with fields Code string, Symbol string and Decimals int, and give CSV, JSON and Markdown a second parameter cur Currency. Totals are in the currency's minor units (cents for USD); write them with cur.Decimals decimal places, and with no decimal point when it is 0. CSV and JSON write the number alone; Markdown puts cur.Symbol before it, as it does with $ today. With Currency{Code: "USD", Symbol: "$", Decimals: 2} the output is what it is now.

name: design-address
prompt: Orders can now ship abroad, so addresses need a country. Give order.Order a field Address of a new type order.Address, with string fields Street, City, Postcode and Country, in place of its Street, City and Postcode fields. shipping.ValidAddress takes an order.Address; it must also report a missing country, and the 5-digit postcode rule applies only when Country is "US". The shipping label ends with the country on a line of its own, except for "US". Everything else, such as the exports, keeps working as before.
